newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks close shade lower in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks close shade lower in consolidation.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed slightly lower on Monday in what brokers called a consolidation following the past two days of gains.
The composite index ended 3.31 points lower at 697.34. It ranged from 697.30 to 706.95.
Affiliates of the troubled Jinro Group fell despite news that the group's prime creditor bank had decided to bail out six of Jinro's 24 affiliates.
Blue chips closed mixed after staying in positive territory for most of the day.
"Selling gained momentum towards the close based on a feeling that the market needed a consolidation early this week," said broker Kim Young-bum of Seoul Securities.

The market rose during the past two trading days on rises of blue chips as the increase in the foreign shareholding limit draws near. The limit is due to rise to 23 percent of a listed firm on May 2 from 20 percent.
Jinro Ltd fell 780 won to its limit of 9,070, Jinro Industries 460 won to its limit of 5,340 and Jinro General Foods 400 won to its limit of 4,600.
Jinro, the nation's 19th largest conglomerate, has said it would sell some of its property and affiliates to raise cash for repayments of its debts valued at 3.2 trillion won.

North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop's arrival in Seoul on Sunday was generally ignored. Hwang, the highest official ever to defect the communist state, sought political asylum on February 12 in Seoul's mission in Beijing.
Brokers predicted the market's movement would be limited to a narrow range on Tuesday as there was a strong selling force awaiting at the symbolic 700-point level.
